record.original_question: Even when the angle is fixed at alpha = pi/4 instead of tending to 0, can one prove a nontrivial lower bound for computing X_(pi/4) in the two-coordinate unitary-step model that is better than (1/(2 sqrt(2))) n log_2 n, which the paper states is the best bound obtainable from the vanilla entropy potential Phi?

evidence.quote: Note that although the main problem proposed here is to understand the asymptotic behaviour of the complexity of X_alpha, as alpha tends to 0, even the case of finding a lower bound for computation of X_pi/4 is not trivial.
It is not clear how (and whether it is at all possible) to get a bound better than 1/(2 sqrt(2)) n log_2 n, which is the best possible using the 'vanilla' entropy function Phi.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let n be a positive even integer. Consider the "two-coordinate unitary-step" computational model for n×n unitary matrices: an algorithm is a finite sequence of elementary steps U_1, U_2, …, U_T, where each U_t is an n×n unitary matrix that acts non-trivially on at most two coordinates (i.e., its restriction to some pair of coordinates {i,j} is an arbitrary 2×2 unitary, and it is the identity on the remaining n−2 coordinates). The algorithm computes the unitary U_T U_{T−1} ⋯ U_1, and its cost is the number of steps T. For an n×n unitary M, let C(M) denote the minimum cost over all algorithms computing M exactly.

For a real angle α, let R(α) = [[cos α, −sin α],[sin α, cos α]] denote the 2×2 rotation, and define the n×n unitary
   X_α = R(α) ⊕ R(α) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ R(α)   (n/2 blocks on the diagonal).

Define the entropy potential Φ on n×n unitaries by
   Φ(U) = ∑_{i,j=1}^{n} h(|U_{ij}|^2),   where h(x) = −x log_2 x   (with h(0)=0).
A standard estimate shows that any single two-coordinate unitary step changes Φ by at most a bounded amount, and using only this potential one can derive the lower bound
   C(X_{π/4}) ≥ (1/(2√2)) · n log_2 n.

Question. Prove or disprove: there exists a constant c > 1/(2√2) such that, for all sufficiently large even n,
   C(X_{π/4}) ≥ c · n log_2 n.
Equivalently, can one establish a lower bound on the two-coordinate unitary-step complexity of X_{π/4} that strictly improves the constant 1/(2√2) obtained from the vanilla entropy potential Φ?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in Ailon's note on the complexity of the Fourier transform in the two-coordinate unitary-step model. Web searches do not surface any subsequent work that improves the 1/(2√2) n log_2 n constant for X_{π/4}; related literature on Ω(n log n) lower bounds in this model has not been reported as having sharpened this specific constant.

status_evidence.title: Interesting Open Problem Related to Complexity of Computing the Fourier Transform and Group Theory
status_evidence.snippet: The goal of this document is to describe a natural open problem that arises from this work, which is related to group theory, and in particular to representation theory.
status_evidence.claim: The bound improvement question for X_{π/4} in the two-coordinate unitary-step model is stated as an open problem.
